facts.statement: Palaeophasianus was an extinct genus of flightless birds belonging to the family Geranoididae that lived in North America during the Eocene.
facts.quote: Palaeophasianus is an extinct genus of flightless Geranoididae birds that lived in North America during the Eocene period.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Palaeophasianus were discovered in 1910 by the American Museum expedition in Big Horn County, Wyoming, within the Willwood formation.
facts.quote: The fossil remains were found by the American Museum expedition of 1910 in Big Horn County, Wyoming, in the Willwood formation (early Eocene).

facts.statement: Robert Wilson Shufeldt described the genus Palaeophasianus in 1913, initially classifying it as a galliform.
facts.quote: Robert Wilson Shufeldt classified Palaeophasianus as a galliform when he described it in 1913.

facts.statement: The classification of Palaeophasianus was later revised, with Pierce Brodkorb moving it to Cracidae in 1964 and Joel Cracraft placing it in Gruiformes in 1968.
facts.quote: However it was transferred to Cracidae in 1964 by Pierce Brodkorb, while Joel Cracraft in 1968 placed it in Gruiformes.

facts.statement: The only known species, Palaeophasianus meleagroides, is described as a ground-dwelling carnivore.
facts.quote: The only species in this genus is P. meleagroides, and it is described as a "ground-dwelling carnivore".

facts.statement: Palaeophasianus lived during the Ypresian stage of the Eocene, between 56 and 51.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 51.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: According to the Paleobiology Database, the parent group of Palaeophasianus is Phasianinae.
The Paleobiology Database lists the family of Palaeophasianus as Phasianidae.
The Paleobiology Database incorrectly classifies Palaeophasianus under the class Reptilia.
